nist-abac.label: NIST
nist-abac.title: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
nist-abac.claim_scope: PAC overlaps with attribute-based access control (ABAC).
nist-abac.why_it_matters: The canonical NIST definition of ABAC — authorization decided by evaluating subject/object/action/environment attributes against policy — is the closest mainstream analog to what PAC evaluates.

nist-zero-trust.label: NIST
nist-zero-trust.title: Zero Trust Architecture
nist-zero-trust.author_or_org: S. Rose, O. Borchert, S. Mitchell, S. Connelly, NIST
nist-zero-trust.claim_scope: Zero Trust's per-resource, per-session authorization model, as an alternative to perimeter trust.
nist-zero-trust.why_it_matters: Zero Trust treats authentication and authorization as discrete decisions made per session against a specific resource, rather than granted by network location — an established authorization-architecture alternative to perimeter trust. It is not evidence about capability-based security, and the document does not describe a per-action authorization model; the comparison is limited to that authorization framing.

opc-ua-part3.label: OPC UA

hse-permit-to-work.label: HSE
hse-permit-to-work.title: Permit-to-work systems
hse-permit-to-work.claim_scope: Authorization is not the same thing as safety.
hse-permit-to-work.why_it_matters: States the exact distinction PAC's own architecture depends on, in an unrelated, decades-old industrial-safety domain: “the issue of a permit does not, by itself, make a job safe.” Also the clearest limit-case for PAC's analogy, since a paper permit assumes a competent human, not an autonomous executor.

oasis-xacml-3.label: OASIS
oasis-xacml-3.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
oasis-xacml-3.claim_scope: XACML's differentiated policy-decision outcomes, as prior art for authorization-outcome semantics — not a claim about PAC's own implementation.
oasis-xacml-3.why_it_matters: XACML distinguishes NotApplicable (no policy applies) from Indeterminate (evaluation failed or conflicted) as separate decision outcomes. PAC's D05 independently returns DEFER for unknown mandatory evidence; the two are not claimed to be equivalent, and this source is not evidence that PAC does or does not match that distinction — that question can only be answered from PAC's own artifacts. XACML is offered here as relevant prior art for thinking about differentiated authorization outcomes.
oasis-xacml-3.verification_status: verified 2026-09-18: fetched/searched, decision semantics confirmed against the official OASIS standard text; wording narrowed 2026-09-18 (007R1) after audit found the original card asserted an unsupported one-to-one/two-to-one mapping onto PAC's own DEFER behavior

w3c-prov.label: W3C
w3c-prov.title: PROV-Overview: An Overview of the PROV Family of Documents
w3c-prov.claim_scope: Provenance, derivation, and lineage representation — not evidence-freshness policy or revocation semantics.
w3c-prov.why_it_matters: PROV is the standards-track model for representing entities, activities, and the agents involved in producing a piece of data — i.e., provenance and lineage, relevant to describing where PAC's evidence came from. It does not define evidence-freshness policy, evidence-age acceptance rules, or revocation ordering/races, which remain open PAC questions this document does not address.

openai-apollo-scheming.label: OpenAI/Apollo
openai-apollo-scheming.title: Detecting and reducing scheming in AI models
openai-apollo-scheming.claim_scope: Controlled evaluations found behaviors consistent with scheming (covert actions used as a proxy) in several frontier models; an anti-scheming training method reduced but did not eliminate them.
openai-apollo-scheming.why_it_matters: Published 17 September 2025. The findings come from controlled test environments; OpenAI states it has no evidence that today's deployed frontier models could suddenly begin significantly harmful scheming, and notes that the most common deployed failures are simpler, such as pretending to have completed a task. Cited as motivation for studying and preserving machine-behavior errors. It does not endorse or evaluate PAC, and PAC's discrepancy classes are not its definitions.
